analyses.predicted_outcome: Preregistered directions come from earlier Gemini-3-Flash / 512 px phases (this board is Gemini 3 at 384 px): H6 (Phase 4, the only untested confirmatory hypothesis) expected the stronger Pro model to transfer/match-or-exceed Flash; H7 (Phase 2b) found T=0.0 optimal for both tracks; H1 (Phase 2a) planned a text-only vs image-using contrast without a committed directional winner. Board result (genuine Pro, all Pro cells n>=3): H6 holds strongly and uniformly -- the top six cells are all genuine Pro, every Pro-text cell beats the best Flash cell (flash-image-minimal-t-0-0, F1 0.600), and the genuine Pro-image cells match Flash on F1 while dominating MCC (any apparent Flash-over-Pro in the raw board traces to the E57 Flash-misdispatched cells, now replaced). H7's T=0.0 optimum is cleanly supported within Pro text: the two Tier-1 cells are both T=0.0 (HIGH and MEDIUM thinking, tied) and the two Tier-2 cells are both T=0.7 -- a clear T=0.0 > T=0.7 ordering at matched model/modality. H1 resolves metric-dependently -- text wins F1@20 m localisation (the top four cells are all text) while image wins MCC tile-discrimination (pro-image-medium-t-0-7, MCC +0.911).
analyses.outcome: At the preregistered 20 m buffer the best single pass for mound localisation is genuine Gemini 3 Pro text at T=0.0. Tier 1 -- the tie_set -- is a two-member statistical tie between pro-text-high-t-0-0 (F1 0.804) and pro-text-medium-t-0-0 (F1 0.792): a round-robin tile-swap permutation (BH-FDR q=0.05; 129/153 pairs significant -> 7 tiers) cannot separate them, and both are significantly clear of the Tier-2 pair -- the two Pro-text T=0.7 cells, pro-text-medium-t-0-7 (0.755) and pro-text-high-t-0-7 (0.745). So at T=0.0 the thinking level (HIGH vs MEDIUM) does not significantly matter, and T=0.0 beats T=0.7 (Tier 1 vs Tier 2) at matched model and modality (H7). The top four cells are all Pro text and the top six all genuine Pro; the text-over-image advantage holds at matched settings (best Pro text 0.804 vs best Pro image 0.666). The F1 leaders are NOT the tile-level discrimination (MCC) leader: genuine Pro IMAGE wins MCC -- pro-image-medium-t-0-7 (MCC +0.911, but 9th on F1) and pro-image-high-t-0-0 (+0.868) -- while Pro text leads F1, so the best single-pass configuration is metric-dependent. (All eight Pro cells are genuine Gemini 3 Pro at n>=3; see deviations E57 and docs/methodology/n1-baseline-matrix.md for board provenance.)

analyses.predicted_outcome: H3: consensus voting over K proposer passes improves localisation F1 over single-pass; the diversity dividend predicts HIGH-thinking (more diverse) pools recover or exceed minimal-thinking under consensus, and that cheap Flash consensus can approach expensive single-pass Pro.
analyses.outcome: Both named claims of the diversity-dividend test are confirmed at the preregistered 20m buffer. Per the registered H3 analysis plan (osf/preregistration.md:519-521: 'Compare single-pass mean F1 vs voted F1 at each (N, threshold) combination' + 'Generate threshold sweep curves' + 'Identify optimal (N, threshold)'), the headline is each configuration's BEST (N, threshold) operating point against the known test-tile ground truth -- the study's purpose is to characterise how well VLM symbol extraction localises mounds, so best-achievable performance is the deliverable, not a confound. Method: round-robin tile-swap permutation (10k perms, seed 42, two-sided; BH-FDR q=0.05) + greedy-clique tiering over a 22-cell board (4 consensus champions + 18 single-pass cells); 197/231 pairs significant -> 7 tiers. (1) DIVERSITY DIVIDEND -- HIGH-thinking consensus significantly exceeds minimal-thinking consensus at matched modality: text +0.153 F1 (BH-p<0.001; MCC +0.239) and image +0.070 F1 (BH-p<0.001; MCC +0.272). The HIGH-thinking pools take the larger consensus gain -- more varied proposals let a high vote threshold prune their false positives. (2) CONSENSUS vs SINGLE-PASS -- every consensus champion significantly beats its matched within-pool single-pass baseline (+0.13 to +0.43 F1, all BH-p<0.001), and the lift persists at the production N=5 operating point (text 4-of-5, image 3-of-5; +0.09 to +0.33 F1). (3) CROSS-ARCHITECTURE HEADLINE -- Tier 1 (the tie_set) is a THREE-member statistical tie: the best Flash HIGH-text consensus (F1 0.814) and the two genuine-Gemini-3-Pro single-pass text leaders (pro-text-high-t-0-0 0.804, pro-text-medium-t-0-0 0.792); the permutation cannot separate Flash-consensus from the Pro leader (p=0.616, BH-p=0.66). Cheap Flash consensus reaches the expensive Pro single-pass tier on localisation F1. OPERATING-POINT SENSITIVITY (characterised, co-headlined): the Tier-1 parity is at the best (N, threshold) point (26-of-30); at the production N=5 carry-forward point (text 4-of-5) the same pool reaches TIER 2 (0.720), tying genuine Pro text at T=0.7 -- a best-minus-N5 delta of ~0.094 F1 (the within-test cousin of the carry-forward-vs-best delta the 55-map generalisation reports). F1-parity is NOT MCC-parity: the Pro text leaders are more tile-precise (MCC 0.790, 11 tile FPs) than the Flash consensus champion (MCC 0.620, 41 tile FPs) -- the metric-dependent-winner pattern of the n1 board persists. Deployment generalisation to unseen maps is the separate question answered by the 55-map runs. Era-2 487-tile test scope, 384px, gemini-3-flash. Artefacts: results/diversity-dividend-384/{tiering-champions,tiering-with-deployable}/tiering_20m.{json,md}; script scripts/consensus_vs_baseline_tiering.py; cell spec planning/diversity-dividend-cells-2026-06-06.json.

analyses.predicted_outcome: H11 (tile size): the prior expectation was non-monotonic with a 384px sweet spot. The refined hypothesis (Obs 351): the optimal tile size shifts with FP-filtering strength — single-pass (no filter) prefers larger tiles; strong filters (HIGH-thinking consensus, consensus+verifier) shift the optimum to 384; 256 falls under every architecture.
analyses.outcome: Tile-size characterisation across 256/384/512 px (F1@20m), gemini-3-flash, GS 4-map curator GT. The optimal tile size is ARCHITECTURE-DEPENDENT, consistent with the FP-filtering mechanism (Obs 351, Obs 179, Obs 171). CLEAN ISOLATION (hold architecture x modality x thinking x temperature constant, vary only size): single-pass text climbs monotonically with tile size (256=0.342 < 384=0.520 < 512=0.606) -- with no FP filter, larger tiles give cleaner proposals; single-pass image is flat (384~0.600 ~ 512~0.586). Text MINIMAL consensus still prefers 512 (+0.02..+0.05 over 384 across T0.3/0.7/1.0) -- a weak filter. Text HIGH consensus FLIPS to 384 (T0.7 0.814 > 512 0.773; T0.3 0.789 > 0.774; T1.0 ~tie) -- the strong diversity+vote filter realises 384's higher recall. CONSENSUS+VERIFIER head-to-head (View 3; Stage-D carry-forward adversarial verifier, gemini-3-flash minimal T=0.0 n=1; 14-buf+MCC; best prob_t per cell): 384=0.890 > 256=0.856 > 512=0.793 -- best=384px (delta +0.034 over 256). Two findings: (1) 384 STILL leads at consensus+PV, as it does at consensus-only, confirming the Obs 179 prior (NOT a surprise); (2) the verifier RESCUES 256 (Obs 352): 256 consensus jumps from 0.460 consensus-only (WORST) to 0.856 consensus+PV (+0.396), LEAPFROGGING 512 to take second -- so the per-architecture order is single-pass 512>384>256, consensus-only 384>512>256, consensus+PV 384>256>512. Obs 351's open question -- does 256 overwhelm even the verifier? -- is now answered: NO, the verifier rescues 256, but 384 retains the lead. CAVEAT: the 256 PV cell is the plain text 5-of-5 (N=5) family, whereas 384/512 share the HIGH-text N=30 lineage (HIGH-text not run at 256), so 256 stays a thin-provenance anchor; tile size is confounded with tile set (1032/487/340), so F1@20m is the cross-size headline and tile-MCC is reported per size, never differenced. BEST-ACHIEVABLE FLASH CEILING per size (consensus-only): 384 (0.814) > 512 (0.775) > 256 (0.460); single-pass 512 (0.631) > 384 (0.520) > 256 (0.342). Pro single-pass ran only at 384 (pro-text 0.792, pro-image MCC 0.868) -- context, not a tile-size comparison. Artefacts: results/tile-size-sweep/tile_size_sweep.{json,md} (now incl. View 3); recon results/era1-pv-stage-d/384-leg-recon.md; script scripts/tile_size_sweep.py.

analyses.outcome: REJECTED on the GS instrument — at equal pass count under PV, MINIMAL reaches statistical parity with HIGH: min6 (n30-lineage, 0.8708) vs high6 (0.8641) p=0.656; min11 (0.8835) vs high11 (0.8769) p=0.591; min11 vs the 31-pass headline (0.8902) p=0.562; min11 vs opmax35 (0.8951) p=0.324; min6 vs min11 p=0.271. The TRUE min6 merge (0.8784) sits numerically above its permuted n30-lineage stand-in. Mechanism (pool_recall_ceilings.json, zero_diversity_anchor.json): the verifier shifts the binding constraint to POOL RECALL; minimal T=0.7 sampling saturates Flash's reachable recall in ~5 passes (0.9195 — the 10-pass lineage adds zero new GT mounds), while HIGH thinking adds volume (union/pass 2.46 vs 1.44) but only +0.023 ceiling. The zero-diversity anchor (1 x T=0.0 pass + n=1 vf) scores 0.8142 with the board's second-best tile-MCC (0.833); min11 holds the best (0.807). The consensus-era dividend (Obs 141) is real for consensus-only architectures and OBSOLETE under PV (Obs 359). SCOPE: GS-characterised only — the parity REVERSED at 55-map deployment (TM-k3 0.8127 T3 vs TH7-k3 0.8425 T1; Obs 362); deployment evidence overrides this characterisation tie.

analyses.outcome: 5 tiers, 20/28 pairs significant after BH-FDR. Board (tile-MCC@50, tier): IM-k3 0.7104 (T1, SOLE leader); T03-k3 (oracle) 0.6903 (T2); TH7-k3 0.6796 (T2); TM-n10-k5 (uplift) 0.6725 (T3); T03-k4 0.6711 (T3); TH7-k4 (carry-forward) 0.6666 (T3); TM-k3 0.6580 (T4); TM-k4 0.6411 (T5). IM-k3 is the SOLE Tier-1 cell — all seven of its pairwise comparisons are significant, including against the F1 oracle T03-k3 (ΔMCC +0.0201, BH p=0.0056). The tier order INVERTS the F1 board at the top (the F1 Tier-4 cell is the MCC sole leader; the F1 oracle drops to MCC T2; only bottom-ranked TM-k4 is invariant), while within the text family MCC still respects the F1 ordering (every k3-above-k4 difference significant) — so the inversion is a MODALITY effect, not noise: the cheap two-call image+verifier stack is the resolved best tile-level discriminator while sitting outside the coordinate-F1 frontier (Obs 369/370). Gate: rebuilt per-tile confusion reproduces the committed Track-2 evaluations exactly, 8/8. 95% CIs are the Track-2 engine's BCa bootstrap MCC CIs.
